data.source_phase_note: Official lme4 documentation identifies days0-1 as adaptation/training and day2 as baseline; the subsequent recorded period has the different study condition. The requested reanalysis uses baseline and all later available days. The original study analyzed reciprocal reaction-time speed and categorical day; this proposed linear reaction-time reanalysis is not a reproduction of that original model. No intervention or individual recommendation is requested.
data.working_model: For each recorded subject g on the analysis days,Reaction[g,t]=beta0+beta1*t+b0[g]+b1[g]*t+epsilon[g,t],where t is source day minus baseline day. Subject random vectors b[g] are independent zero-mean Gaussian with one common unconstrained2x2 covariance G; errors are independent N(0,sigma2) across visits and subjects and independent of b. beta is a fixed unknown mean,not a distribution of population identities. Estimate G and sigma2 by restricted maximum likelihood(REML) on this explicitly declared linear Gaussian working model; no claim that the historical sample is representative or model assumptions are empirically proved. Retain all complete subjects and their full requested trajectories.
data.balanced_likelihood_note: With a common full-rank two-column X=[1,t] for every subject,let A=(X^T X)^-1 and beta_g be each subject OLS vector. The restricted likelihood factorizes into the between-subject coefficient covariance Sigma=G+sigma2*A and the orthogonal within-subject residual variance. The unconstrained estimates are sample covariance of beta_g using subject_count-1,and pooled within-subject SSE/[subject_count*(visits_per_subject-2)]. Recover G=Sigma-sigma2*A only if it is positive semidefinite; otherwise a constrained covariance fit is required rather than silently accepting negative random variance. A general correct REML implementation is scientifically equivalent to the applicable balanced closed form. This is a model definition/method identity,not supplied fitted coefficients or variances.
data.reporting_definitions: Let delta=final_analysis_day-baseline_day. fixed_mean_change_ms=delta*beta1; its plug-in standard error is abs(delta)*sqrt(Sigma[1,1]/subject_count),where slope is the second coefficient. between_subject_latent_change_sd_ms=abs(delta)*sqrt(G[1,1]) excludes measurement error. same_subject_observed_difference_sd_ms=sqrt(delta^2*G[1,1]+2*sigma2) includes two independent endpoint errors. baseline_final_observation_correlation=(G[0,0]+delta*G[0,1])/sqrt((G[0,0]+sigma2)*(G[0,0]+2*delta*G[0,1]+delta^2*G[1,1]+sigma2)). Do not replace any of these distinct quantities by one common residual SD. Preserve source subject columns as the coefficient/data basis; visit equation rows can reorder jointly.

source_provenance.attribution: lme4 sleepstudy dataset,original Belenky et al.(2003) reference retained in official dataset documentation. Original article was not read in full.
source_provenance.format_export: Every original180 Reaction/Days/Subject observation is retained as a10day by18subject matrix with explicit source factor labels and day codes. This is a lossless table pivot,not fitted values,selected outcomes or new experimental data. No latent effects,random covariance,residual estimates or answer fields are supplied.
source_provenance.decoder: rdata0.11.2 pure-Python original RDA decoder; no R code execution.

provenance.kind: Public historical records and/or explicitly disclosed derived audit inputs; source-specific provenance is in the study record. Controlled numerical teaching fixtures make no experimental observation claim.
